name: Pickleball Fundamentals
tagline: Master the basics and build a solid foundation
description: Perfect for complete beginners! This 14-day comprehensive program covers everything you need to start playing pickleball with confidence. Each day includes instructional videos, guided drills, and clear practice goals.
keyOutcomes: Master proper continental grip and ready position
Execute consistent serves with 80%+ success rate
Return serves deep into the court consistently
Develop foundational dinking skills at the kitchen line
Understand basic court positioning and strategy
Learn complete rules and scoring system

dailyStructure.title: Grip, Stance, and Ready Position
dailyStructure.focus: Building the foundation for all pickleball shots
dailyStructure.description: Today we start with the most important fundamentals: how to hold the paddle and position your body. These basics will support every shot you learn throughout the program.

warmup.title: Dynamic Warmup
exercises: Shoulder circles forward and backward (10 each)
Mini paddle swings without ball (20 reps)
Shadow swings in ready position (15 reps)

main_drills.name: Grip Check
main_drills.description: Practice the continental grip: Hold paddle like shaking hands. Check that you can see 'V' formed by thumb and index finger pointing to top of paddle edge.
tips: Grip should feel natural, not strained
Don't choke up too high on the handle
Maintain same grip for forehand and backhand

main_drills.name: Ready Position Reps
main_drills.description: Stand in athletic stance: feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, weight on balls of feet, paddle up in front. Hold for 10 seconds, relax, repeat.
tips: Keep paddle head up at chest level
Stay light on your feet
Look straight ahead, not down at ground

main_drills.name: Movement Drill
main_drills.description: From ready position, practice shuffle steps: 3 steps right, return to center, 3 steps left, return to center. Maintain ready position throughout.
tips: Don't cross feet - use shuffle step
Paddle stays in ready position while moving
Explode from your legs, not reaching with arms

practice_goals: Master the continental grip and can demonstrate it confidently
Hold ready position for 30 seconds without breaking form
Complete all movement drills while maintaining proper stance
Watch both instructional videos fully and understand key concepts
success_metrics: Can explain and demonstrate continental grip
Can hold ready position for 30+ seconds
Complete all warmup and drill repetitions
dailyStructure.coach_notes: Don't rush! These fundamentals seem simple but they're crucial. Every pro player maintains perfect grip and ready position. If you master these today, everything else will be easier. Take your time and focus on feeling natural in this position.

age_adaptations.youth: Keep sessions shorter (20 min). Make it fun with games - 'freeze' game to practice holding ready position.
age_adaptations.adult: Standard progression works well. Focus on building muscle memory through repetition.
age_adaptations.senior: Take extra breaks. If knees hurt, slightly higher stance is okay. Focus on balance and stability.

dailyStructure.title: Forehand Groundstroke Basics
dailyStructure.focus: Developing a consistent and controlled forehand
dailyStructure.description: The forehand is your most important shot in pickleball. Today we learn proper technique for a reliable forehand groundstroke that you can count on in every game.

main_drills.name: Wall Rally - Forehand Only
main_drills.description: Stand 10 feet from a wall. Hit gentle forehands against the wall, focusing on form not power. Let ball bounce once before hitting.
tips: Turn your body sideways before swinging
Point non-paddle hand at ball as it approaches
Follow through across your body, finish high
Contact ball in front of your body, not beside you

main_drills.name: Target Practice
main_drills.description: Set up targets (cones, towels, etc.) in different areas of court. Try to hit forehands to specific targets. Focus on control.
main_drills.reps_or_sets: 50 total shots (10 to each of 5 targets)
tips: Aim for consistency over power
Watch the ball all the way to your paddle
Keep same swing speed - don't muscle it
Hit through the ball, don't push or poke

practice_goals: Execute 50 forehands with proper turning and follow-through
Hit 5 forehands in a row against wall without missing
Land 30+ shots in desired target areas
Maintain continental grip throughout all drills
success_metrics: Achieve 5+ consecutive wall rallies at least once
dailyStructure.coach_notes: Power comes later - today is all about developing the right motion. Think 'smooth' not 'hard'. Your follow-through is more important than your backswing. If balls are flying wild, slow down and exaggerate your follow-through to your target.

age_adaptations.youth: Use softer balls if available. Focus on fun and consistency games: 'How many can you hit in a row?'
age_adaptations.adult: Standard progression. If arm gets tired, take 2-minute breaks between sets.
age_adaptations.senior: Use lighter paddle if available. Shorter swings with focus on placement over power. Take breaks as needed.

gender_tips.general: Everyone should focus on technique before power. Smooth beats hard every time.
gender_tips.power_focus: You might be tempted to hit hard immediately - resist! Build technique first, add power in weeks 2-3.
gender_tips.finesse_focus: Your natural touch is an advantage. Focus on paddle control and placement.

dailyStructure.title: Backhand Groundstroke Basics
dailyStructure.description: Many beginners struggle with backhands, but a solid two-handed backhand is actually easier to learn than a forehand. Today we develop this crucial shot.

main_drills.name: Two-Handed Backhand Wall Rally
main_drills.description: Stand 10 feet from wall. Hit two-handed backhands, focusing on smooth shoulder rotation. Let ball bounce once.
tips: Both hands on paddle, dominant hand on bottom
Turn shoulders so chest points to side wall
Lead with bottom hand, guide with top
Finish with paddle in front of opposite shoulder

main_drills.name: Alternating Forehand-Backhand
main_drills.description: Hit against wall alternating shots: forehand, backhand, forehand, backhand. Focus on transitioning between shots.
tips: Return to ready position between shots
Recognize forehand vs backhand quickly
Same grip for both shots (continental)
Stay balanced and controlled

practice_goals: Execute 50 two-handed backhands with proper rotation
Alternate between forehand and backhand smoothly
Hit 5 backhands in a row against wall
Feel comfortable with backhand grip and stance
dailyStructure.coach_notes: The two-handed backhand is often stronger than the forehand for beginners! Let your shoulders do the work, not just your arms. Think 'turn and follow through' - that's it. Don't over-complicate it.

dailyStructure.title: Basic Serve Technique
dailyStructure.description: In pickleball, the serve must be underhand and below the waist. Today we master this fundamental serve that starts every point.

warmup.title: Serving Warmup
exercises: Practice serve motion without ball (10 slow, 10 fast)
Ball drops - practice dropping ball smoothly (10 reps)

main_drills.name: Serve Form Practice
main_drills.description: Practice serve motion: feet behind baseline, drop ball, swing paddle low-to-high below waist, contact ball at or below waist level.
tips: Drop ball with non-paddle hand
Don't throw ball up - just drop it
Swing path is low to high
Contact point at or below your waist
Follow through toward your target

main_drills.name: Deep Serve Practice
main_drills.description: Serve from behind baseline trying to land ball deep in service box (within 3 feet of baseline). Alternate sides (deuce/ad).
tips: Aim for back half of service box
Deep serves are harder to attack
Consistent depth > perfect placement
Find rhythm - same motion every time

practice_goals: Execute 50 legal serves (all below waist, all underhand)
Land 30+ serves in the correct service box
Develop consistent ball drop and swing rhythm
Serve at least 15 balls deep (back half of service box)
success_metrics: Achieve 60%+ success rate (30+ in service box)
dailyStructure.coach_notes: The serve is your only shot where you have complete control. Develop a repeatable routine: step up, bounce ball twice, take a breath, drop and swing. Same routine every single time. Consistency comes from routine.

dailyStructure.title: Service Return Fundamentals
dailyStructure.description: The return of serve is the second most important shot. A good return puts you in control of the point. Today we learn to return serves deep with confidence.

warmup.title: Return Warmup
exercises: Shadow returns - forehand and backhand (10 each)

main_drills.name: Self-Feed Returns
main_drills.description: Stand at baseline. Drop-feed yourself balls (simulate incoming serves) and practice returning deep to opposite baseline.
tips: Start in ready position
Use split step as ball is served
Turn early and prepare paddle
Return deep - aim for back 1/3 of court
Follow your return to kitchen line

main_drills.name: Partner Return Drill
main_drills.description: Partner (or ball machine) serves to you. Practice returning serves consistently deep. Alternate forehand and backhand sides.
tips: Read spin on incoming serve
Block back hard serves, drive soft serves
Aim for opponent's backhand corner
Move forward after returning

practice_goals: Return 25+ serves into opponent's court
Land 15+ returns in back 1/3 of court (deep)
Develop split step timing
Feel comfortable returning to both forehand and backhand sides
dailyStructure.coach_notes: A deep return is more important than a perfect return. Your goal is to keep the serving team back so you can get to the kitchen line. Don't try to hit winners - just get it back deep and move forward. The kitchen line is where you want to be.

dailyStructure.title: Introduction to the Kitchen (Non-Volley Zone)
dailyStructure.focus: Understanding and practicing at the kitchen line
dailyStructure.description: The kitchen (non-volley zone) is where most points are won and lost. Today we learn the rules, positioning, and basic shots from the kitchen line.

warmup.title: Dinking Warmup
exercises: Practice soft touch bounces (tap ball gently 10 times)
Ready position at kitchen line practice

main_drills.name: Kitchen Rules Quiz
main_drills.description: Learn and practice: Can't volley in kitchen, can step in after bounce, both feet must be out to volley. Practice stepping in and out.
tips: Kitchen line extends infinitely to sides
Any part of foot on line = violation
Momentum carries count as violations
Can stand in kitchen any time - just can't volley there

main_drills.name: Wall Dinking
main_drills.description: Stand 3-4 feet from wall. Hit very soft shots that arc over 'net' (mark on wall) and land just beyond kitchen line distance on wall.
tips: Use minimal backswing
Very soft touch - let paddle absorb ball energy
Arc ball over net (not straight line)
Keep paddle face slightly open

main_drills.name: Partner Cross-Court Dinking
main_drills.description: Both players at kitchen line. Hit soft dinks cross-court to each other. Goal: keep rally going as long as possible.
main_drills.reps_or_sets: Try to reach 10+ shot rallies, 5 times
tips: Stay patient - resist urge to speed up
Keep ball low over net
Soft hands - cushion the ball
Watch ball all the way to paddle

practice_goals: Understand all kitchen rules completely
Hit 30+ successful dinks (ball lands in opponent's kitchen)
Achieve at least one 10-shot dinking rally
Develop soft touch and paddle control
dailyStructure.coach_notes: Dinking is pickleball's most unique and important skill. The best players in the world spend hours dinking. It's not boring - it's strategic. Master the soft game first, then add speed. 'Soft is the new hard' in pickleball.

dailyStructure.title: Rest Day & Review
dailyStructure.description: Rest is crucial for learning and muscle recovery. Today we review what we've learned through mental practice and light movement.

warmup.title: Light Movement
exercises: Easy walk or light jogging (5 minutes)
Shadow swings - all shots learned so far (slow motion)

main_drills.name: Mental Practice
main_drills.description: Sit comfortably and visualize yourself performing each shot perfectly: grip, ready position, forehand, backhand, serve, return, dink. See and feel each motion.
tips: See yourself from outside view (like watching video)
Then switch to first-person view (your eyes)
Feel the motion in your muscles
Visualize successful outcomes

practice_goals: Complete light movement and stretching
Mentally review all 6 days of training
Visualize successful execution of each shot learned
Feel refreshed and ready for week 2
success_metrics: Journal or notes about week 1 progress
dailyStructure.coach_notes: Rest is not laziness - it's when your brain consolidates learning. Studies show that mental practice (visualization) is nearly as effective as physical practice. Use today to let your muscles recover while your mind reinforces everything you learned this week. Come back tomorrow fresh!

dailyStructure.title: Volley Basics
dailyStructure.focus: Developing consistent forehand and backhand volleys
dailyStructure.description: Volleys (hitting balls before they bounce) are crucial for fast-paced exchanges. Today we learn proper volley technique for both forehand and backhand.

warmup.title: Volley Warmup
exercises: Quick feet drills (high knees, butt kicks)
Ball taps - soft touch practice (20 taps)

main_drills.name: Wall Volleys
main_drills.description: Stand close to wall (3-4 feet). Hit continuous volleys without letting ball bounce. Alternate forehand and backhand. Focus on compact swing.
tips: Minimal backswing - think 'block' not 'swing'
Paddle stays in front of body
Use continental grip for both sides
Quick short punches

main_drills.name: Partner Volley Drill
main_drills.description: Both players stand inside baseline. Feed balls to each other (non-volley zone) and practice consistent volleys. Start slow, gradually increase pace.
tips: Stay on balls of feet
Watch ball to paddle
Firm wrist - don't let paddle droop
Aim for consistency not power

practice_goals: Execute 100+ successful volleys
Maintain continuous volley rally of 20+ shots
Develop compact, efficient volley motion
Feel comfortable with both forehand and backhand volleys
success_metrics: Achieve at least one 20+ volley rally
dailyStructure.coach_notes: Volleys are all about preparation and reaction time. The less you swing, the quicker you can react. Think 'punch' not 'swing'. Keep paddle in front, stay ready. Speed comes from quick feet, not big swings.
